docs.title: Docs-As-Code Project
docs.text:
Welcome to the Docs-As-Code Project documentation portal.

This website demonstrates how to create, manage, and publish technical documentation using:

  • Markdown
  • MkDocs
  • Material for MkDocs
  • GitHub
  • GitHub Actions
  • GitHub Pages

docs.title: About This Project
docs.text:
Docs-as-Code is an approach where documentation is treated like source code.

Key principles:

  • Write documentation in Markdown
  • Store documentation in Git
  • Review changes using Pull Requests
  • Automate builds using CI/CD
  • Publish documentation as a website

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
This documentation portal includes:

  • Easy navigation
  • Search capability
  • Version control
  • Responsive design
  • GitHub integration
  • Automated deployment

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before using this project, ensure that you have:

  • Python installed
  • Git installed
  • GitHub account

docs.title: Install MkDocs
docs.text: pip install mkdocs

docs.title: Install Material Theme
docs.text: pip install mkdocs-material

docs.title: Run the Website
docs.text:
mkdocs serve

Open your browser and navigate to:

http://127.0.0.1:8000

docs.title: User Guide
docs.text:
The User Guide explains how to:

  • Navigate the documentation
  • Search content
  • Access API references
  • Submit feedback

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
To contribute:

  1. Create a new branch.
  2. Update Markdown files.
  3. Commit your changes.
  4. Create a Pull Request.
  5. Request review.

docs.title: Support
docs.text:
For questions or issues:

  • Create a GitHub Issue
  • Contact the Documentation Team

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text:
Welcome to the Docs-As-Code Project.

This guide helps you set up the documentation portal on your local machine and preview the website using MkDocs.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before you begin, ensure you have the following installed:

  • Python 3.10 or later
  • Git
  • A code editor such as Visual Studio Code

docs.title: Project Structure
docs.text:
Docs-As-Code/
│
├── mkdocs.yml
│
└── docs/
    ├── index.md
    └── getting-started.md

docs.title: Install MkDocs
docs.text:
Install MkDocs and the Material theme:

pip install mkdocs mkdocs-material

Verify the installation:

mkdocs --version

docs.title: Create the Documentation Site
docs.text:
Start the local development server:

mkdocs serve

Open the following URL in your browser:

http://127.0.0.1:8000

docs.title: Create Your First Page
docs.text:
Create a new Markdown file:

docs/user-guide.md

Add the following content:

# User Guide

Welcome to the User Guide.

docs.title: Update Navigation
docs.text:
Edit the mkdocs.yml file:

nav:
  - Home: index.md
  - Getting Started: getting-started.md
  - User Guide: user-guide.md

Save the file and refresh the browser.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
After completing the setup:

  • Create additional documentation pages
  • Push the project to GitHub
  • Configure GitHub Pages
  • Set up GitHub Actions for CI/CD deployment

docs.title: Summary
docs.text:
You have successfully:

  • Installed MkDocs
  • Created a documentation site
  • Started a local server
  • Added a
